limitations: Provider verification describes deployed contract capabilities and does not expose an MDK reader or writer.
A router convenience quote and an exact state-changing eth_call have different meanings and must be returned as different result types.
Provider availability and historical-state retention are per endpoint and must not be inferred from chain identity.

quote.meaning: A block-scoped router calculation for one amount and exact route. It is neither exact-call simulation nor a guaranteed minimum received.

execution.payer: msg.sender; transferFrom sends input directly to the first pool
execution.recipient: the explicit to argument; intermediate pool outputs go directly to the next pool
execution.nativeValue: zero for the evidenced ERC-20 exact-input route
execution.factoryRule: A zero factory tuple selects defaultFactory; every nonzero factory must be approved by factoryRegistry, and every resolved pool must be recognized before a route is usable.

quote.meaning: The router ABI exposes execution entrypoints but no standalone Quoter. Pool math may produce an estimate with explicit assumptions; only an eth_call of the exact intended entrypoint is an exact-call simulation.

execution.payer: msg.sender for the first hop; the router pays subsequent exactInput hops from intermediate balances held by the router
execution.recipient: the explicit recipient; a zero recipient resolves to the router and is not a safe user default
execution.nativeValue: route-dependent; zero for the evidenced ERC-20/native-token-address exactInputSingle transaction
execution.factoryRule: Each hop resolves from the immutable CL factory by sorted tokens and int24 tick spacing, and the callback validates the computed pool.
